FAKE-SYNTHETIC demo visit note: synthetic data, roles only.
Visit notes, Lakeside Community Health 098 (Minnesota; corporate owner). General acute is the main facility type. Met the pharmacy director and the immunization lead at the hospital outpatient pharmacy.

Scale first: about $665K in net dollars, roughly a tenth of the in-state total among the synthetic peers and a small slice of national dollars. The pharmacy director wanted that size context on one line before we moved on.

RSV leads the mix at close to two fifths of dollars, well above the national share, with a high index. We walked the must-cover dollar share of RSV in detail, and the immunization lead agreed the general acute sites are where that volume concentrates. I asked what is driving purchasing in RSV and which programs are planned for next season. They described a hospital outpatient protocol and a planned winter review, and they want a short national-index leave-behind.

Switching was straightforward: no material switching between the two windows, and they did not dispute that.

We also covered the meningococcal must-cover in full: MenB plus MenABCWY to MenACWY plus MenABCWY doses is about double the in-state peer ratio. The immunization lead had questions about that index and asked for the peer n to be printed on the page.

Rotavirus came up only in passing. The pharmacy director said the name was on their list but they were not ready to talk about the dollar share versus the national file, did not want to walk the index today, and asked to park that point for a later call. I noted it as incomplete and did not press.

The MSA is live into late 2027 and does not renew automatically. I will send the RSV and meningococcal pages this week and hold the parked item for the next visit.
